fields.name: aggregatedPostMetrics
fields.description:
Aggregate normalized post metrics across a filtered post set. Useful
for yearly summaries, channel-level rollups, and BI exports without
paginating through thousands of posts.

For per-post metrics, use `posts(input)` or `post(input)` with a
`metrics { … }` selection — this query is purely for aggregation.

The result always contains a baseline trio of entries: `postCount`
(number of matched posts in the window), `reactions`, and `comments`.
Posts on networks that don't track reactions or comments contribute 0
to those totals.

Beyond the baseline, additional metric types are returned only when
every channel in the filter set supports them. A single-network filter
surfaces that network's richer metrics (e.g. impressions, reach,
engagementRate on LinkedIn); a mixed-network filter trims the extras
to those common to every network in the set.

fields.name: createContentItem
fields.description:
Create a content item together with all of its channel-specific post variants
in a single operation. Validation is all-or-nothing: if any variant fails
validation, no content item and no variants are created. Variants that fail
while being processed after creation are reported per channel in the failure
payload; the content item and its variants are still created in that case.

This API is an early preview and can change without a deprecation period.

fields.name: createContentItemDraft
fields.description:
Create a content item holding a channel-less draft, before any channels
are selected. No network-specific validation applies to the draft content.
The draft needs text or at least one asset.

This API is an early preview and can change without a deprecation period.

fields.name: deleteContentItem
fields.description:
Delete a content item: the item itself and any posts created from it.
Deletion is all-or-nothing. Every post must be deletable on its own, or
nothing is deleted and every blocked post is reported at once. A post can
only be deleted while it is a draft, awaiting approval, scheduled, or
failed, so an item cannot be deleted while any of its posts is publishing
or already published. An item still holding a channel-less draft has no
posts, so nothing blocks it. An error can also be reported when a post
could not be fully processed after the deletion already took effect;
re-fetch before retrying.

This API is an early preview and can change without a deprecation period.

fields.name: promoteContentItemDraftToPosts
fields.description:
Promote a channel-less draft into channel-specific posts. One-way: once
promoted, the content item can no longer be edited as a draft. If any post
fails validation, none are created. A failure can also be reported when a
post could not be fully processed after the promotion already took effect;
re-fetch the content item to check its state before retrying.

This API is an early preview and can change without a deprecation period.

fields.name: removePostFromContentItem
fields.description:
Remove a post from a content item. The post survives on its own channel
and keeps its schedule, text, status, and tags. Only the link to the
content item goes away. To delete a post, call deletePost.

A second call with a post that belongs to no content item changes nothing,
and the mutation reports success.

fields.name: updateContentItem
fields.description:
Update a content item's title or target date. Fields that are

This API is an early preview and can change without a deprecation period.

fields.name: updateContentItemDraft
fields.description:
Replace a channel-less draft's content in full, and optionally set the
content item's target date in the same write. The draft needs text or at
least one asset. Only valid while the content item is still a draft.

This API is an early preview and can change without a deprecation period.

fields.name: createTag
fields.description:
Create a tag for an organization.

The name must be unique within the organization; a duplicate is refused with
`DuplicateError`. Creation is refused with `LimitReachedError` once the
organization already holds as many tags as its plan allows.

This API is an early preview and can change without a deprecation period.

args.name: input
args.description:
Identifies the organization to create the tag in, and the name and color to
give the tag.

fields.name: deleteTag
fields.description:
Delete a tag.

The tag is removed from every post, idea and content item carrying it; those
items are otherwise untouched. A locked tag can be deleted, and deleting an
unlocked tag frees a slot for the oldest locked one. See `Tag.isLocked`.

This API is an early preview and can change without a deprecation period.

fields.name: updateTag
fields.description:
Update a tag's name and color.

Both values are replaced, so send the current value for the one you are not
changing. The new name must still be unique within the organization; a
duplicate is refused with `DuplicateError`.

A locked tag cannot be edited and the update is refused. See `Tag.isLocked`.

This API is an early preview and can change without a deprecation period.

args.name: input
args.description: Identifies the tag to update, and the name and color to set on it.

types.name: PostMetricType
types.description:
List of possible metrics available for a Post.

Values fall into three groups:
- **Cross-network normalized** (reactions, comments, shares, reposts, reach, impressions, views, clicks, engagementRate): Used wherever a concept maps cleanly across networks. Per-network adapters normalize their native names (e.g., Instagram `likes` → `reactions`, Twitter `retweets` → `reposts`).
- **Network-specific** (saves, follows, quotes, viewers, totalTimeWatched, averageTimeWatched, likes, freeSubscriptions, paidSubscriptions): Real metrics that don't have a cross-network equivalent. `likes` is intentionally distinct from `reactions` on Facebook — Facebook's Graph API surfaces them separately. `freeSubscriptions` and `paidSubscriptions` are Substack's per-Note subscription attribution; no other network reports it.
- **Aggregation-only** (postCount): Meaningful only on aggregate endpoints; never emitted per-post.

Deprecated values are pre-normalization legacy or tied to features being removed. They're kept in the enum for backwards compatibility until clients migrate.

enumValues.name: averageTimeWatched
enumValues.description: Average time watched, in seconds, for video-style posts (TikTok, Instagram Reels).

enumValues.name: clicks
enumValues.description: How many times people clicked on your post.

enumValues.name: comments
enumValues.description: The count of comments and replies on your post. Unified across networks (Threads `replies` maps here).

enumValues.name: engagementRate
enumValues.description: The percentage of people who interacted with your post compared to how many saw it. Unit: percentage.

enumValues.name: favorites
enumValues.description: Deprecated: not emitted by any per-network definition. Use `reactions` instead — Twitter and Mastodon favorites normalize into `reactions`. Will be removed on 2026-12-01.

enumValues.name: follows
enumValues.description: The number of new followers gained from this post (Instagram).

enumValues.name: freeSubscriptions
enumValues.description: The number of free subscriptions Substack attributes to this Note.

enumValues.name: impressions
enumValues.description: How many times your post was shown on screen. May include multiple views by the same person — useful for spotting how often the content gets surfaced.

enumValues.name: likes
enumValues.description: The Like-reaction subcount on Facebook. Distinct from `reactions` (which is the total of all reaction types — Like, Love, Care, Haha, Wow, Sad, Angry); Facebook's Graph API reports them separately and we mirror that.

enumValues.name: link_clicks
enumValues.description: Deprecated: StartPage link-clicks metric. StartPage is being deprecated as a product. Will be removed on 2026-12-01.

enumValues.name: other
enumValues.description: Deprecated catch-all from pre-normalization. Never emitted. Will be removed on 2026-12-01.

enumValues.name: paidSubscriptions
enumValues.description: The number of paid subscriptions Substack attributes to this Note.

enumValues.name: postCount
enumValues.description: The count of posts included in an aggregated response. Only meaningful on aggregate endpoints — never emitted per-post.

enumValues.name: quotes
enumValues.description: How many times your post was quoted (Threads).

enumValues.name: reach
enumValues.description: The number of unique people who saw your post.

enumValues.name: reactions
enumValues.description: How many people reacted to your post. Unified across networks: Instagram/Twitter `likes`, Mastodon `favorites`, etc. all map to this value.

enumValues.name: reblogs
enumValues.description: Deprecated: not emitted by any per-network definition. Use `reposts` instead — Mastodon reblogs normalize into `reposts`. Will be removed on 2026-12-01.

enumValues.name: repins
enumValues.description: Deprecated: not emitted by any per-network definition. Pre-normalization legacy from the Pinterest era. Will be removed on 2026-12-01.

enumValues.name: replies
enumValues.description: Deprecated: not emitted by any per-network definition. Use `comments` instead — replies are normalized into `comments` on the networks that distinguish them (Threads). Will be removed on 2026-12-01.

enumValues.name: reposts
enumValues.description: How many times your post was reposted by others. Twitter `retweets`, Mastodon `reblogs`, Threads `reposts` all normalize to this value.

enumValues.name: retweets
enumValues.description: Deprecated: not emitted by any per-network definition. Use `reposts` instead — Twitter retweets normalize into `reposts`. Will be removed on 2026-12-01.

enumValues.name: saves
enumValues.description: How many times people saved your post (Instagram, Pinterest). A strong signal that the content is worth revisiting.

enumValues.name: shares
enumValues.description: How many times your post was shared or forwarded by others.

enumValues.name: totalTimeWatched
enumValues.description: Total time watched, in minutes, for video-style posts (LinkedIn, TikTok, Instagram Reels).

enumValues.name: viewers
enumValues.description: Unique viewer count for video-style posts (LinkedIn).

enumValues.name: views
enumValues.description: How many times your post was viewed. Used for video-style posts and on networks that report views distinctly from impressions.

types.name: ContentItemAction
types.description:
Actions the calling actor can take on a `ContentItem`. The server computes
this set from the same rules the content item mutations enforce. A client
reads it to drive UI affordances instead of deriving the rules itself.

The set carries an action only when a client can offer it on this one item.
An action whose answer is the same for every item in a response drives no
affordance, so it stays out. Read access is one of those: the API returns
only a content item the actor may read.

enumValues.name: deleteContentItem
enumValues.description:
The actor can delete this content item. An item that holds channel-specific
posts gets a second check. The mutation checks each post, so a delete can
still fail.

enumValues.name: updateContentItem
enumValues.description:
The actor can change this content item's title and target date. The actor
can also change the tags and the draft text while the item holds a
channel-less draft.

in it, rather than being per channel or per person.

fields.description:
Stable Buffer palette identifier derived from `color`.

fields.name: isLocked
fields.description:
Whether the tag is locked.

A tag locks when the organization holds more tags than its plan allows,
typically after a downgrade. Buffer locks the excess rather than deleting it,
so nothing is lost if the organization upgrades again.

A locked tag **cannot be edited** — `updateTag` rejects it. It can still be
read, deleted, and applied to posts through the API. Buffer's own apps also
hide locked tags when picking a tag for a post; that is a client convention,
not something the API enforces.

Locking is recalculated when the organization's plan changes, and deleting an
unlocked tag frees a slot for the oldest locked one.

types.name: __Schema
types.description: A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description: If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields`, `interfaces`, and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

types.name: __Field
types.description: Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description: Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and optionally a default value.

fields.name: defaultValue
fields.description: A GraphQL-formatted string representing the default value for this input value.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description: One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned in a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.
